instruction: How does the JS event loop prioritize microtasks?
output: After each macrotask (timer, I/O), the loop drains the entire microtask queue (promises, queueMicrotask) before the next macrotask — so `Promise.resolve().then(...)` always beats `setTimeout(..., 0)`. Starving microtasks (infinite promise chains) freeze rendering; break them with awaits on real timers.

```js
const [a, b] = await Promise.all([getA(), getB()]); // gagal jika salah satu gagal
const hasil = await Promise.allSettled([getA(), getB()]); // {status, value|reason} setiap satu
```
all = fail-fast parallelism; allSettled = bulk jobs where partial success is fine; race = timeouts (`Promise.race([kerja, timeout(5000)])`). Never sequential-await independent promises in a loop.

```js
const bandar = pengguna?.alamat?.bandar ?? "Tidak tahu";
```
`?.` short-circuits on null/undefined instead of throwing; `??` defaults only for null/undefined (unlike `||`, which also swallows 0, "" and false). Pair them for safe deep access with honest fallbacks.

```js
const debounce = (fn, ms) => { let t; return (...a) => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => fn(...a), ms); }; };
```
Debounce waits for silence (search inputs, resize end); throttle caps rate (scroll handlers, mousemove). Both need cancel methods in components — leaked timers are a top SPA memory-leak source.

instruction: Map vs Object and Set for dedupe?
output:
```js
const unik = [...new Set([1, 2, 2, 3])]; // [1, 2, 3]
const cache = new Map();
```
Map allows any key type and preserves insertion order with O(1) size; plain objects coerce keys to strings (`{}[{}]` collides). Set dedupes primitives in one line — for object arrays, dedupe by key via Map.

instruction: What does TypeScript strict mode buy me?
output: Strict mode (`"strict": true`) turns on null checks, no-implicit-any and strict property initialization together — catching at compile time the undefined-is-not-a-function crashes that plague JS. Turn it on for every new project; migrating old code, enable flags one by one starting with `strictNullChecks`.

Interfaces describe object shapes and merge on repeat declaration (good for extending libs); `type` aliases cover unions, tuples and primitives. Rule: `interface` for public object contracts, `type` for everything else. Both vanish at runtime — never rely on them for validation.

instruction: When do I use unknown instead of any?
output: Always prefer `unknown` for untrusted data (API responses, JSON.parse): unlike `any`, the compiler forces narrowing (`typeof x === "string"`) before use. `any` silently disables checking and spreads — treat every `any` as tech debt with an expiry date.

output: Use `tsx` for dev/run (esbuild-powered, near-instant, handles ESM+TS); `ts-node` is slower and fiddly with ESM. Ship with `tsc` emit for type-checked builds. So: tsx while coding, `tsc --noEmit` in CI for checking, `tsc` for the production bundle.

instruction: TypeScript types vanish at runtime — so how do I validate API input?
output: Compile-time types erase, so validate at boundaries with a schema library (zod/valibot): parse once, get both runtime safety and inferred static types. Never trust `as` casts on network data — casts assert without checking. One schema at each system edge beats dozens of defensive checks inside.

instruction: When do I use TypeScript never?
output:
```ts
function mustahil(x: never): never { throw new Error("tak tercapai"); }
```
`never` untuk kod yang tidak sepatutnya jalan — semakan exhaustiveness switch: `default: mustahil(nilai)` gagal compile jika kes baharu tiada pengendalian. Jangan keliru dengan `void` (pulang undefined).

instruction: What does the satisfies operator do?
output:

```ts
const cfg = { port: 3000, hos: "x" } satisfies Config;
```
`satisfies` semak objek menepati jenis TANPA luaskan jenisnya — autolengkap kekal literal (`3000`, bukan `number`). Alternatif `as Config` senyap buang maklumat jenis literal.

instruction: Show a Dockerfile for a Node.js app.
output:
```dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
USER node
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```
Copying package files first lets Docker cache the dependency layer so it is only rebuilt when dependencies change.

Set `"type": "module"` in package.json for `import` syntax; without it Node uses CommonJS `require`. ESM supports top-level await and static analysis; mixing needs `createRequire` shims. New projects: ESM throughout, `.cjs` extension only for legacy files.

Use `npm ci` in CI/Docker: strict lockfile install, fails on mismatch, wipes node_modules first — reproducible. `npm install` updates the lockfile and tolerates drift — for dev machines. Rule: ci in pipelines and images, install on workstations.

instruction: How do I set up Tailwind CSS?
output: Install the CLI (`npm i -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli`) with `@import "tailwindcss";` in your CSS, or the classic config route (`tailwindcss init`, content paths, directives). The engine scans source files and generates only used utilities — production CSS stays kilobytes, not megabytes.

instruction: What is utility-first CSS in Tailwind?
output:
```html
<button class="rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 font-bold text-white hover:bg-blue-700">Simpan</button>
```
Style by composing small utilities in markup instead of naming custom classes. Reads verbose at first, but eliminates dead CSS, naming debates and specificity wars — the stylesheet is generated from what you actually use.

instruction: How do responsive prefixes work in Tailwind?

instruction: How do I do dark mode in Tailwind?
output: Use class strategy (`darkMode: "class"` in v3; v4 `custom-variant dark`) so a `.dark` ancestor toggles: `<div class="bg-white text-black dark:bg-black dark:text-white">`. Pair with the app's theme store + `prefers-color-scheme` default. Never ship dark: variants without a toggle — half your users get the wrong theme.

```css
.btn-utama { @apply rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 text-white; }
```

Use @apply for genuinely repeated component patterns to cut markup noise — but overuse recreates the custom-CSS problems Tailwind removes (dead code, specificity). Rule: three repetitions of identical utility chains earns an @apply or a framework component.

instruction: Why is my Tailwind production CSS huge?
output: The `content` paths miss your templates, so nothing purges — set them to cover every file with classes (`./src/**/*.{html,js,ts,jsx,tsx}`).
